purpose: Negative control fixtures for the clean-machine harness contract. Each case describes an injected fault, the stage that must detect it, the detection predicate, and the expected_error code the harness must report. A validator must be able to reproduce every case deterministically and must fail if any case produces a green.

cases.injection: After cloning at the pinned base commit, modify a tracked file (for example append a byte to package.json) before any stage runs.
cases.detection: git status --porcelain in the workspace is non-empty, or resolved HEAD does not equal the pinned base_commit.
cases.expected_behavior: The run aborts before toolchain stage and labels the run invalid with DIRTY_BASE.

cases.injection: Pre-populate the dependency/build cache on the host and configure the harness to restore it, but strip the provenance record (no key, source, content hash, or producer run id).
cases.detection: A cache hit exists in the run evidence whose record lacks any required provenance field, or a cache was consumed without any cache record at all.
cases.expected_behavior: Even with all stages exiting zero, the run is rejected as clean-machine evidence with CACHE_LEAK; it may only be labeled developer_local.

cases.injection: Run on a host image with cmake removed from PATH (or node absent).
cases.detection: A required tool reports not-found, or its observed version violates the declared pin.
cases.expected_behavior: The toolchain stage fails naming the missing tool and the violated pin; the run aborts before dependencies.

cases.injection: After npm ci completes, add an extraneous package to node_modules (for example npm install left-pad@1.3.0 --no-save) or delete an installed package directory.
cases.detection: Post-install dependency-tree fingerprint differs from the lockfile-derived expectation recorded at stage start.
cases.expected_behavior: The dependencies stage fails with DEPENDENCY_DRIFT naming the fingerprint mismatch; build never starts.

cases.injection: Inject a failing assertion into one deterministic unit test (or force native/build.ps1 -RunTests to fail by breaking a fixture).
cases.detection: Any stage command exits non-zero; the evidence record carries the exit code, failing names, and log tail.
cases.expected_behavior: The run stops at the failing stage and is labeled invalid with NONZERO_STAGE; no later stage may run.

cases.injection: Start the built server, then make cleanup skip termination of its PID (simulating a crashed or forgotten child).
cases.detection: Post-cleanup listener enumeration finds a tracked PID still alive or still holding a capsule port.
cases.expected_behavior: The process stage (or cleanup verification) reports LEAKED_PROCESS with pid, process name, and held port; the host is not safe to destroy and the run is invalid.

cases.injection: Launch the server with a configuration that binds 0.0.0.0 (or any address other than 127.0.0.1) inside the capsule range.
cases.detection: Observed listener table for the launched PID shows a bind address other than 127.0.0.1.
cases.expected_behavior: The launch stage fails immediately with NON_LOOPBACK_BIND naming the process, port, and observed address; the process is terminated as tracked and the run is invalid.

cases.injection: Set the server (or smoke client) target port to 6500 — the owner-reserved live server port — via config, command line, or environment default.
cases.detection: Any launch argument, configuration value, environment default, or observed listener references port 6500, regardless of bind address.
cases.expected_behavior: The run fails with FORBIDDEN_PORT_6500 before or at launch; this failure is never waivable and is reported at P0 on every platform.

validator_requirements: Every case must be reproducible from its injection description alone.
A harness version passes validation only when all eight cases produce their expected_error and no case produces a green run.
Positive control: the unmodified pipeline on a fresh disposable host must produce zero expected_error codes and label the run clean_machine_verified.
